newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money stays at 10.53125 pct.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money stays at 10.53125 pct.

text.p: * Volume rises to 21.517 bln from 9.495 bln pesos
Manila overnight money stayed at an average rate of 10.53125 percent on Monday even after banks had covered three days of weekend positions, traders said.
"There were so many lenders. It was easy to borrow," said a dealer from a big bank.
Rates ranged from 10.625 to 10.53125 percent, with 32 lenders and 24 borrowers.
Banks, meanwhile, were buying bills on expectations interest rates would further dip after the Central Bank closed today its five-month special series T-bills which had been offered at 10.90 percent.
That five-month bill served as a floor for comparable bills, a trader said.
The Central Bank, instead, offered 38-day special series T-bills at 10.5 percent, dealers said.
Banks were also looking forward to investing their money in the primary auction of T-bills later in the day, dealers said.
A Reuter poll of six institutions show them with bid rates of 10.625/10.70 for three-months bills; 10.85/10.925 for six months; and 11.30/11.45 for one year.
